output.brief: The evidence points to Callerby's own decision as the main cause of the slip. The tower crane was taken off site on 20–22 October 2025 for the Kestrel job. It stayed away until April. The lender's independent surveyor records that level 3–4 steel was delivered and ready to erect from 21 October, and that no frame erection happened until the crane returned. CO-09 was a small change: four beams on level 2, installed in December with a hired mobile crane. The other change orders were fit-out items with float. The platform's tamper-proof log shows the architect answered 62 of 64 RFIs within the contract period. The 41 "late" RFIs in the draft claim were mostly sitting in Callerby's own drafts. I am fairly confident (roughly 80–90%). Open points are whether the Kestrel incentive drove the crane move, and what a fair split of the delay is. Do not submit the claim as drafted. It rests on a flawed measure and invites a counterclaim. Do not discipline the superintendent. He answered truthfully, and punishing him would suppress information. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet. Instead, withdraw the claim, negotiate the final account, and review how the crane transfer was approved. Consider separate advice on any narrow, genuine claim, such as the CO-09 beams.
